summary: Army tower near Roy, Pierce County, dated 1942 by firelookout.com; WillhiteWeb could not confirm it existed; the possible site is on Joint Base Lewis-McChord land.

facts.status_note: Firelookout.com marks it abandoned; the Washington Lookouts index marks it removed; the FFLOS list marks it gone. WillhiteWeb could not confirm that a lookout existed here.

access.note: Fort Lewis land, now Joint Base Lewis-McChord (military reservation). The Fort Lewis page says access needs permission ('Permission is possible'); no source describes public access to this site.

events.note: Dated only by firelookout.com ('1942: tower'). WillhiteWeb could not find evidence that a lookout existed in the area.

evidence.supports: four miles northwest of Roy, Pierce County
firelookout.com mentions the 1942 tower; WillhiteWeb could not find evidence
evidence.quote: Firelookout.com makes mention of this abandoned 1942 tower possibly located near the Ninety-first Division Prairie.

evidence.supports: WillhiteWeb found no evidence of a lookout in the vicinity of the firelookout.com location
evidence.quote: any evidence of a lookout existing in the vicinity of where it was located on the website
Nor could I find any staff that had any knowledge of this lookout

evidence.supports: possible lookout on the 10th Field Artillery Bluff, unconfirmed
evidence.quote: The 10th Field Artillery Bluff offers an excellent view of the Ninety-first Division Prairie so I wouldn't be surprised if one certainly existed on the bluff.

evidence.supports: uncertain whether the Nisqually Lookout existed
evidence.quote: Of the 6 possible locations, 5 lookout sites were found, but one (the Nisqually Lookout) I am still uncertain as to its existence.

evidence.supports: Fort Lewis land now Joint Base Lewis-McChord
evidence.quote: This page highlights the former lookouts located on Fort Lewis lands, now known as Joint Base Lewis-McChord.

evidence.supports: author had access to these spots in late summer 2013 while working for the Army
evidence.quote: I found access to these spots while working for the Army as a Forestry Technician & wildland firefighter during the end of summer 2013.

evidence.supports: access needs permission; permission is possible
evidence.quote: Do not attempt access without permission. Permission is possible.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com gives a 1942 Army tower four miles northwest of Roy. WillhiteWeb says the author could not find evidence of a lookout there and is uncertain it existed. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Very thin record. The 1942 date rests only on firelookout.com, and WillhiteWeb doubts the lookout existed, so the 1942 event is typed 'other' (dated tower) rather than 'built'. Staff and fires: none found. The WashingtonLookouts index lists the owner as 'U. S. Army' and status 'Removed'. Access 'restricted' is inferred from the base status and the Fort Lewis page's permission advice; no source describes public access to this site. The brief's status 'gone' is consistent with all three listings. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the story's lead now attributes the tower to firelookout.com instead of stating it existed, and the 'went looking' and 'nearby bluff' details were removed as unsupported.
